newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bonds start key data week little changed.
newsitem.headline: Australia bonds start key data week little changed.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were little changed from Friday's levels as the market braced itself for this week's key events -- the AIRC's "living wage" claim verdict and the quarterly CPI.
*U.S. Treasury yields off slightly amid consolidation.
Australian bond yields were little changed from Friday's levels as the market braced itself for this week's key events -- the AIRC's "living wage" claim verdict and the March quarter CPI.
Both events could stir thoughts of a further easing in monetary policy given that the economic recovery has turned patchy and particularly if the wages outcome proves subdued.
The market rallied strongly last week, taking their yields to the lowest for 1-1/2 months, in anticipation that these two events will be bond friendly.

Economists expect the Australian Industrial Relations Commission to set the "living wage" outcome at A$12 per week on Tuesday, which is not seen concerning the Reserve Bank as far as future wage inflation growth.

This verdict would be above the government's proposed A$8 per week, but below the A$20 per week pay increases over the next three years, and the 8.75 percent minimum award this year, put foward by the Australian Council of Trade Unions.
Wednesday's March quarter headline CPI is seen rising just 0.1 percent and the underlying rate by 0.4 percent, according to a Reuter survey of economists.

Local yield spreads to the U.S. widened slightly after U.S. Treasury yields eased amid consolidation following its recent bear run. Currency considerations saw Canadian bonds underperform the U.S. as the Canadian dollar weakened, while N.Z. firmed against Australia on a strengthening N.Z. unit.
